text_to_speech: In this unit, we will review some words related to astronomy - the study of stars, planets and space. [MUSIC] Altitude is the angular position of a celestial body in relation to the observer’s horizon, measured in degrees. Apogee is a point in the orbit of the moon or any such satellite that is farthest from the centre of a planet. Perigee: is a point in the orbit of the moon or any such satellite that is nearest to the centre of the planet. Ascension: is an astronomical term used to measure the angular distance of a celestial object with reference to a point on the celestial equator and the earth’s equator. Asteroids are large rocks, the size of minor planets that orbit the sun. Millions of asteroids orbit in the asteroid belt located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. Astronomer: is an expert who observes celestial objects and other celestial phenomena. Astronomical: is an adjective that refers to anything related to the field of astronomy. Azimuth: is the angular distance of a celestial body from the north or south point of the observer’s horizon. Comet: is a small icy object that orbits the sun and has a long tail of gas and dust. Conjunction: happens when two planets or celestial objects appear to be in the same position in the sky. Constellation: is a group of stars that form a recognizable pattern in the sky. The Orion or hunter constellation is shown here. Cosmogenic: is an isotope of a material produced by the action of cosmic rays. Cosmogony: is the study of the origin of the universe. Cosmography: is a branch of science that deals with the physical features of the universe. Cosmology: is a branch of astronomy dealing with the origin of the universe. Declination: is the angular distance of a celestial object in relation to the earth. Epoch: is a phase in the development of the universe after the Big Bang. Equinox: refers to the two days in year when the nights and days are of equal length. This happens at the time the sun crosses the celestial equator. Solstice: refers to either of the two days in a year when the sun is farthest from the celestial equator. Galaxy: consist of billions of stars and planets held together by gravitational force. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way, contains in the range of 100-400 billion stars. Horizon: is the boundary where the sky appears to meet the land. Latitude: is any parallel circle, located on either of the hemisphere of the earth, that runs east to west and is parallel to the equator. Lodestar: is a star that acts as a guide in the sky during navigation. Luminosity: is the actual brightness of energy radiated by a star per unit time Meteor: is a rock that enters the earth’s atmosphere and appears to be shining due to the heat produced by friction. Meteoroid: is a former stage of a meteor before it enters the earth’s atmosphere. Nadir: is a point on a celestial sphere that is located directly below the observer. Zenith: is a point on a celestial sphere located directly above the observer. Navigation: refers to celestial navigation or astronavigation which involves determining the position of celestial bodies by using the sun, moon, and stars as reference points Nebula: is a massive cloud of dust and gases in outer space that is the birthplace of new stars. Observatory: is a building that houses huge scientific telescopes from which observations are made to study astronomical and meteorological phenomena. Parsec: is an astronomical unit to measure distance equal to 3.26 light years. Planetarium: is a domed building in which informative videos and presentations about astronomical phenomena are displayed. Quadrant: is an instrument used to measure angular distance between celestial objects. The quadrant is the ancestor of the more contemporary sextant, which is still used today by some nautical navigators. Satellite: is a celestial body that orbits around a planet; also refers to an artificial device that is positioned to orbit around the earth to collect and relay information. Sidereal: is an adjective that means of or relating to the stars or constellations Star: a celestial body that emits light that is generated by nuclear reactions in its center. Syzygy: happens when three celestial bodies, like the sun, moon, and earth, are in a straight-line configuration. Tropic : refers to any of the two parallels in the celestial sphere that correspond to the northern and southern passages of the sun. We have the tropic of cancer and tropic of capricorn
